title: Tuberculosis as a Wikipedia disease node
dek: Q12204 is a disease graph: cause, site, test-class, and drug-therapy edges. It is not a regimen, a DST, or a lesion PK model.
story: English Wikipedia's Tuberculosis article (Wikidata Q12204) is a disease node: an airborne mycobacterial disease with pulmonary and extrapulmonary forms, an infection-versus-disease split, and a cloud of historic names (phthisis, consumption). That is useful as a glossary. It is not where a lab should learn 2HRZE, BPaLM, or a critical concentration.

The sitelinks and Wikidata edges are the pedagogical object. Q12204 points at Mycobacterium tuberculosis as a cause, at IGRA/TST as infection tests, at GeneXpert-class NAATs as disease diagnostics, and at a P2176 drug-or-therapy list that is historically incomplete (isoniazid, rifampicin, PZA, EMB, PAS, ethionamide, cycloserine, capreomycin, viomycin — not bedaquiline, pretomanid, or linezolid on the snapshot used here).

Simplfy already has clinic plates for diagnosis, first-line, DR definitions, and TPT. This card exists to pin the encyclopedia graph onto those ids: Wikipedia names the node; WHO names the regimen; WGS names the allele.
deepTitle: How to read a disease page without turning it into a protocol
deep: Wikidata P2176 (drug or therapy used for treatment) is a sparse, curator-lagging edge. Absence of bedaquiline on that list is not evidence against BPaLM. Presence of viomycin is not a licence to build a 2024 backbone around a barely used peptide.
Incidence and mortality numbers on a Wikipedia infobox are time-stamped journalism, not a surveillance extract. Cite WHO Global TB Report when a number has to move a programme.
The infection/disease split on the page maps onto TST/IGRA versus mWRD/culture. Do not let the article's lead sentence collapse those test classes.
Historic synonyms (phthisis) still appear in 19th-century autopsy series and in OCR of sanatorium ledgers. They are aliases, not ICD codes.

visual.caption: Q12204 sits above infection-versus-disease, then above test class, then above the lab objects Simplfy already treats as plates. Wikipedia is the top glossary row.

example.title: A P2176 list is not Group A
example.setup: A student pastes Wikidata's drug-therapy edge for tuberculosis and asks why bedaquiline is missing and viomycin is present.

steps.title: Name the edge
steps.body: P2176 is 'drug or therapy used for treatment' as curated on Wikidata. It is not WHO's Group A/B/C ranking and not a national essential-medicines list.

steps.title: Do not invert absence
steps.body: Bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid are first-class DR-TB drugs in WHO modules. Their absence on a Wikidata snapshot is lag, not evidence.

steps.title: Do not invert presence
steps.body: Viomycin is a historic peptide cousin of capreomycin. Seeing it on Q12204 does not put it on a 2024 all-oral backbone.

example.takeaway: Wikipedia/Wikidata name the disease node. WHO names the backbone.

check.prompt: What is Wikipedia's Tuberculosis article (Q12204) licensed to teach in this studio?
choices: The current WHO BPaLM composition and doses
A glossary and graph of the disease node, not regimen grammar
Critical concentrations for BDQ on MGIT
That IGRA-positive means culture-positive pulmonary TB
check.answer: A glossary and graph of the disease node, not regimen grammar
check.why: The plate's contract: encyclopedia for names, WHO/CDC for protocol.

whyWrong.The current WHO BPaLM composition and do: That lives on the BPaLM clinic plate, sourced to WHO.

check.prompt: Wikidata P2176 for Q12204 lists isoniazid and viomycin but not bedaquiline. The correct reading is:
choices: Viomycin is Group A and BDQ is obsolete
P2176 is an incomplete historic therapy edge; WHO Group A still centres BDQ/Pa/LZD for eligible DR-TB
Wikipedia supersedes WHO when they disagree
Q12204 is a species, not a disease
check.answer: P2176 is an incomplete historic therapy edge; WHO Group A still centres BDQ/Pa/LZD for eligible DR-TB
check.why: Count the edge as a graph, not as a formulary.

whyWrong.Wikipedia supersedes WHO when they disag: The studio ranking is WHO then CDC then Wikipedia.
whyWrong.Q12204 is a species, not a disease: Q12204 is the disease; Q130971 is the organism.

check.prompt: On the hierarchy plate, which row is the encyclopedia object rather than a Simplfy clinic plate?
choices: The bottom row labelled Simplfy plates
The top row labelled Wikidata disease / Q12204 TB
The mWRD cell, which is a WHO cartridge
check.answer: The top row labelled Wikidata disease / Q12204 TB
check.why: The figure is a stack: glossary node, then states, then tests, then existing plates.

whyWrong.The mWRD cell, which is a WHO cartridge: That is a test class, not the disease QID.
